steps.title: Near Cape Town
steps.body: Stellenbosch lies about 50 km east of Cape Town, in the Western Cape. It's surrounded by mountains, like the Simonsberg, Helderberg and Stellenbosch Mountain, with vineyards on slopes and valley floors. It has about 13,000 hectares of vines and around 150 wineries. Soils are mostly ancient granite and sandstone, among the oldest in the wine world.

steps.title: Mediterranean with ocean breezes
steps.body: Stellenbosch has a warm Mediterranean climate: dry summers, wet winters. False Bay, just to the south, sends cool sea breezes inland in the afternoon. The Cape Doctor, a strong south-easterly wind, cools vines and keeps them healthy. Mountain slopes add altitude and different exposures, so sites vary greatly.
steps.highlight: False Bay breezes and the Cape Doctor

steps.prompt: What cools Stellenbosch vineyards in the afternoon?
steps.explanation: False Bay lies just south of the region.

steps.title: History
steps.body: Stellenbosch was founded in 1679 by Simon van der Stel, the Dutch governor of the Cape, making it South Africa's second oldest town. French Huguenots arrived in the 1680s with winemaking skills. Stellenbosch University, home of the country's main wine science department, created Pinotage in 1925. The Wine of Origin system began in 1973.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Stellenbosch lies among mountains east of Cape Town
False Bay breezes and the Cape Doctor cool it
